correctness.rationale: The exact stationary Poisson-age representation gives covariance (2D/r)(g_N-(1-pi/4)a_N^2). Joint Gaussian order-density integration gives E[A_N B_N]=0,-sqrt(3)/pi,-3/pi for N=2,3,4 and exact means a_2,a_3,a_4. A Gaussian Ornstein-Uhlenbeck interpolation, coordinatewise positive association and opposite-monotone covariance imply 0<=g_N<=1/N for every N>=2; since a_4>1 and 1-pi/4>1/5, all N>=5 are strictly negative. Classical normal maximum bounds plus Gaussian Poincare prove the covariance and correlation limits. Proof covers all quantified physical parameters; standard-library diagnostic quadratures check N=2 through 8 and all exact small-N identities. No finite enumeration is used as proof of the universal statement.

value.rationale: For the same stationary physical gas, the natural macroscopic observables are leftmost/rightmost particle positions. Although coordinates remain linearly uncorrelated, their extrema change from positive to strictly negative covariance at an exact and unexpectedly small particle number N=4. The all-N proof and asymptotic correlation -1 quantify common-age-driven anticorrelation in the thermodynamic limit, beyond a textbook identity or arbitrary numerical slice. The result is a precise finite-size effect relevant to interpreting extreme spatial fluctuations under global resetting, without claiming a dynamical phase transition.
